$comment: The source of sf-chart-scatter (standard simai.smart-component 1.3.14 in the 1.4 form, vocabulary 1.1.5). The parameters are docs/research/catalogue.md of ui-chart (Scatter / bubble) and docs/research/parameters.md §1, the keyboard docs/research/rendering.md §3.1, the renderer D5, the name the owner's M2 plan of 2026-11-03 (docs/DECISIONS.md D9).

label.summary: What the chart shows, in a few words: its accessible name and the table's caption. Required in practice: without it the chart is named «График».

items.summary: The data: a list of records, one point each ([{country, income, life}, …]), or an object of columns. A row without both measures is no point; the summary says how many were left out.

names.summary: What each series is called, by its key: {eu: «Европа»}. A series without a name is called by its key.

colors.summary: What colour each series is, by its key: {fact: 'primary', plan: 'neutral'}. A colour is a Framework role (primary, secondary, tertiary, neutral, success, warning, error, info), which follows the theme, or any CSS colour or variable; anything else is dropped with a console report, as is a colour under 3:1 against the background (drawn all the same). A series without one keeps the palette by its place. In forced colours a series is its dash.

palette.summary: The seriess' colours as a named set, by place, each a light and a dark tone that change with the theme and hold 3:1 against surfaces 0-2: theme (the theme's own tones, as before), vivid (8, the first the brand's), soft (8, muted), warm (6), cool (6), brand (4 steps of the primary family, for ordered data). Past its size a set starts again. colors wins for the seriess it names.

x.summary: The field of the horizontal measure; the first numeric field when unset.

y.summary: The field of the vertical measure; the next numeric field when unset.

bubble.summary: The field of a third measure, drawn as each point's area: the points become bubbles. A value of zero, below zero or missing has no area and is drawn as a small ring.

series.summary: One series per distinct value of this field, each its own colour and mark; one series when unset.

point.summary: The field that names each point (a country, a product); the tooltip, the live line, the table and the summary say it. A point without one is called by its row.

x-min.summary: The start of the horizontal axis; the data's own when unset.

x-max.summary: The end of the horizontal axis; the data's own when unset.

y-min.summary: The start of the vertical axis; the data's own when unset.

y-max.summary: The end of the vertical axis; the data's own when unset.

x-zero.summary: The horizontal axis takes zero in.

y-zero.summary: The vertical axis takes zero in.

trend.summary: linear draws each series' least-squares line across its points, dashed. The summary always says the strength of the relation (Pearson's r), with or without the line.

legend.summary: auto shows the legend above the plot when there are two series or more. Each entry is a button that hides and shows its series.

tooltip.summary: point: under the pointer or the cursor, the point's name and its measures.

grid.summary: Which guide lines the plot draws across it.

x-label.summary: The name of the horizontal measure, said under the axis and in the tooltip, the table and the summary; the x field's name when unset.

y-label.summary: The name of the vertical measure, said above the axis and in the tooltip, the table and the summary; the y field's name when unset.

bubble-label.summary: The name of the bubble's measure, said in the tooltip, the table and the summary; the bubble field's name when unset.

x-format.summary: The horizontal measure's format: number, integer, decimal-<n>, percent (a share 0..1), compact, currency-<CODE> or unit-<unit>, in the page's language.

y-format.summary: The vertical measure's format: number, integer, decimal-<n>, percent (a share 0..1), compact, currency-<CODE> or unit-<unit>, in the page's language.

bubble-format.summary: The bubble measure's format: number, integer, decimal-<n>, percent (a share 0..1), compact, currency-<CODE> or unit-<unit>, in the page's language.

size.summary: The rung of the size ladder: the plot's height, the text and the gaps. 1/2 for a card, 2 for a page of its own.

table.summary: The same data as a table: toggle offers a button that swaps the plot for it, visible shows it under the plot, hidden keeps it for screen readers only. Never none: the table is the chart's text.

summary.summary: auto: a sentence of what the data does (the points' count and ranges, the bubbles' range, each series' relation with its strength and direction, the highest and lowest named point), said before the plot. The description slot adds the host's own words.

data-state.summary: auto: ready with points, empty without. loading draws the frame without marks; error offers «Повторить», which sends refresh.

hidden-series.summary: The keys of the series the person hid with the legend.

toggle.summary: The person hid or showed a series with its legend button; applied at once (the vocabulary's local toggle).

select.summary: The person chose a point: a click on it, or Enter or Space on the keyboard cursor. index is the point's row in items, point its name ('' without the point field).

refresh.summary: The person asked for the data again from the error state; the host loads it and sets items.

reset.summary: Shows every series again and takes the cursor away.

description.$comment: The host's own words about the chart: said with the summary (aria-describedby) and shown under the plot.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16); the plot is SVG, its marks on a canvas under it past 2,000 (D5).

skeleton.$comment: The items arrive after the first paint when the host loads them: the derived skeleton holds the plot's box (its height is the size rung's) until they do (standard 1.3.8 §5.4).

accessibility.x-keys: The plot is one Tab stop (role group, aria-roledescription «точечная диаграмма»). Left and Right move the cursor to the point before and after in reading order (by x, then y), so every point is reached; Up and Down to the nearest point above or below; Home and End to the ends; Page Up and Page Down a tenth at a time, past 200 points Left and Right a hundredth. Each move is said in a polite live region: the point's name and its measures. Enter and Space choose the point (select); Escape takes the cursor away. The legend entries and the table button are buttons of their own.

x-summary: A scatter chart: one point per row at two measures, to show how they go together, with an optional third measure as a bubble's area, series by colour and mark shape, a least-squares trend line on request, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor that walks the points, a summary in words with the strength of each relation, and the same data as a table.
x-decisions: name: sf-chart-scatter, the Framework's naming rule sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>], block chart (the owner's M2 plan of 2026-11-03; docs/DECISIONS.md D9), family chart; reserved by the dispatcher in ui-control control/decisions/2026-11-02-ui-chart-package.md.

bubble: a variant of the scatter through a field (catalogue.md), not a chart of its own. The field is bubble, not size as parameters.md first named it: size is the size rung on every chart of the package.
data: items with a field mapping x, y, bubble, series and point (D3); one point per row, never aggregated; a row without both measures is left out and counted in the summary.
a bubble's area, not its radius, is in proportion to its value, against the largest value; a value of zero, below zero or missing has no area and is a small ring.

renderer: own SVG (D5); past 2,000 marks the marks are drawn on a canvas under the SVG, which keeps the axes, the cursor and every text in the accessible tree. The canvas takes its colours from probes in the series' classes, so a role, a palette and forced colours come out as the page has them, and it is painted again when the page's theme changes.

colour is never the only cue: a series past the first has its own mark's shape (circle, square, triangle, diamond, a triangle down); bubbles stay circles and their series differ by an outline's dash in forced colours.

keyboard: the arrows of rendering.md §3.1 for a scatter. Left and Right walk the reading order (by x, then y), so every point is reached; Up and Down go to the nearest point above or below, as Datawrapper's.
summary: the relation of each series is said in words with Pearson's r (none under 0.1, weak under 0.3, moderate under 0.7, else strong), whether the trend line is drawn or not.
select: {series, index, point, x, y}, since a point has two measures and no x of a series; index is the row in items.
table: never none; one row per point in the data's order.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-chart-scatter to show how two measures of the same things go together (income and life expectancy of countries, price and sales of products), and a third as bubbles.
do_not: Do not draw a chart without a label
Do not use it for a series along time; that is sf-chart-line
Do not use bubbles where the third measure must be read precisely; give it in the table or a bar chart
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-chart-scatter label="Доход и продолжительность жизни" x="income" y="life" point="country"></sf-chart-scatter>

accessibility.focus: One Tab stop on the plot, then the legend buttons and the table button. The summary is the plot's description; each cursor move is said politely.

$comment: The chart draws its empty and error states as sf-empty-state; a tag it renders is a tag it fetches.
Its own buttons (the legend, the table toggle) are native buttons, so it fetches no sf-button.
